Good morning, my fellows ketoers,

I've been on keto since July 2013. No cheat at all, maybe 2 quick "accidents". The loss of weight has been high during the first weeks then it's been flat.

My balance tells me I'm remaining around 19% fat so even if I gain weight, it's actually water that I have trouble getting rid of. I've been followed by an endocrinologist all that time because of an increasingly difficult autoimmune condition., We don't know what gives me chronique fatigue and fibromyalgia but it looks like Crohn's disease along with maybe my Mum's diagnosed Lupus and Sjögren's syndrom.

Anyway I'm quite happy at the moment and I observe that my weight drops whenever I get some sun light. It increases when it's cloudy, raining or the temperature drops, which makes me a walking barometer. Maybe that's about the Gilbert/Maulengracht syndrome which makes it harder to metabolize D-vitamin.

I don't know if keto's good to me but I've gotten used to it, to the point of being disturbed by anything sweet. I like my Chardonnay dry and my sparkling wine "brut". I also enjoy red wine but I actually don't drink in the evening if I have to work the day after.

I developed many recipes (I luckily enjoy cooking a creative way) and enjoy cooking my pumpkin seed flour bread, and also cocoa flour-based quiches.

The greatest thing about keto is the way one enjoys fat once we learn to: I remember flying across the Atlantic whilst eating small portions of butter and drinking fresh Merlot. This and the fact I was reading a 700 pages book about the history of mathematics made this otherwise awful trip a nice souvenir.

My keto milestones were the following:

  1. knowing what not to eat
  2. Enjoying it
  3. Not missing the forbidden rest
  4. properly ordering at a restaurant
  5. Having my friends getting used to my food habits without hassling them (I'm popular at birthday party as everyone begs me to swapmy piece of cake for their cups of Champagne)
  6. Even having healthy colleagues trying it for some time, then suddenly turning into fitter persons and getting their gratitude

I'll keep doing keto for as long as I cannot do enough sport to allow me a cheat day, but then, I don't desire these foods we only take on cheating days.

Finally I recently read about someone who would be one of the most famous ketoers, at least when it comes to drinking: Lemmy
